questions.text: Does the system perform social scoring of natural persons by public or private actors?
questions.help: Social scoring means evaluating or classifying persons based on social behaviour or personal characteristics, leading to detrimental treatment.

questions.text: Does the system use real-time remote biometric identification in publicly accessible spaces for law enforcement?
questions.help: This covers live facial recognition and similar biometric identification deployed in public areas.

questions.text: Does the system exploit vulnerabilities of specific groups (age, disability, social situation) to materially distort behaviour?
questions.help: Subliminal techniques or exploitation of vulnerabilities causing harm are prohibited under Art. 5.

questions.text: Is the system used as a safety component of critical infrastructure (energy, transport, water, digital)?
questions.help: AI systems that are safety components in the management and operation of critical infrastructure are classified as high-risk (Annex III).

questions.text: Is the system used in education or vocational training to determine access, assign, or assess students?
questions.help: Systems that determine access to education, evaluate learning outcomes, or assess appropriate levels of education (Annex III, 3).

questions.text: Is the system used in employment, worker management, or recruitment (CV screening, interview evaluation, task allocation)?
questions.help: AI systems for recruitment, selection, HR decisions, task allocation, or monitoring of workers (Annex III, 4).

questions.text: Is the system used to evaluate creditworthiness or establish credit scores of natural persons?
questions.help: Except for systems used to detect financial fraud (Annex III, 5b).

questions.text: Is the system used by law enforcement for individual risk assessment, polygraph, evidence reliability, or crime prediction?
questions.help: AI systems used by law enforcement authorities for profiling, crime analytics, or risk assessment (Annex III, 6).

questions.text: Is the system used in migration, asylum, or border control for risk assessment or document authentication?
questions.help: AI used to assess risks posed by persons entering the EU or for verifying document authenticity (Annex III, 7).

questions.text: Is the system used in the administration of justice or democratic processes?
questions.help: AI used to assist judicial authorities in researching, interpreting facts and law, or applying the law (Annex III, 8).

questions.text: Does the system interact directly with natural persons (e.g., chatbot, virtual assistant)?
questions.help: Systems that interact with persons must disclose they are AI (Art. 52 transparency obligation).

questions.text: Does the system generate or manipulate images, audio, or video content (deepfakes)?
questions.help: AI-generated or manipulated content must be labelled as such (Art. 52).

PROHIBITED.label: Prohibited
PROHIBITED.description: This AI system falls under practices prohibited by Art. 5 of the AI Act. It cannot be placed on the EU market.

HIGH_RISK.label: High Risk
HIGH_RISK.description: This AI system is classified as high-risk under Annex III. It must comply with mandatory requirements including risk management, data governance, transparency, human oversight, and conformity assessment.

LIMITED_RISK.label: Limited Risk
LIMITED_RISK.description: This AI system has transparency obligations under Art. 52. Users must be informed they are interacting with AI, and generated content must be labelled.

MINIMAL_RISK.label: Minimal Risk
MINIMAL_RISK.description: This AI system is classified as minimal risk. No mandatory requirements apply, but voluntary codes of conduct are encouraged.
